sources.title: Ultimate Research Queue for 2.x
sources.basis: Current portal and public source inspection found a maintained MIT custom research GUI and queue owner, but only a queue-read remote interface and no supported presentation-extension contract. Integration requires an upstream hook or another stable public contract, not private GUI mutation.

intake.document_authority: Proposed brief accepted as task scope; technical assertions require exact independent evidence.

requests.title: Hide infinite research in game
requests.rationale: A personal display filter must not change force research availability.
requests.implementation: Add All / Finite / Infinite view modes using technology metadata; keep actual force queue and technology state unchanged.
acceptance: Two players in one force select different modes with identical research availability
Setting survives reload without prototype mutation
remaining_obligations: Configuration change, mod removal and conflict capture
Full route omission explanations remain in Inspector; native browser detail shows actual ingredients and effects

requests.title: Show only infinite research in game
requests.rationale: Use one mutually exclusive tri-state filter, not conflicting hide/show switches.
requests.implementation: Classify infinite tails, finite configured caps and upgrade-series entries explicitly; add text search and availability filter.
remaining_obligations: Configuration change, mod removal and conflict capture
Full route omission explanations remain in Inspector; native browser detail shows actual ingredients and effects

requests.title: Native research-screen/queue buttons and queue-mod interoperability
requests.proposed_scope: Bundled browser; native filter requested upstream
requests.rationale: The inspected custom-GUI API does not establish permission to rewrite native research-screen internals.
requests.implementation: Use a shortcut and a supported relative anchor where actually available; expose a bounded query for cooperating queue mods; never require them.
acceptance: Optional integration absent causes no startup failure
remaining_obligations: Configuration change, mod removal and conflict capture
Full route omission explanations remain in Inspector; native browser detail shows actual ingredients and effects

requests.title: Grouped settings and one row per technology
requests.proposed_scope: Grouped viewer/editor for runtime settings; restart-required profile export
requests.rationale: An in-game UI can organize controls but cannot make startup prototype settings hot-editable or redesign the native main menu.
requests.implementation: Render enable/cost/scaling/cap columns from existing SettingSpec; show effective value, origin, target applicability and restart badge; export only validated sparse overrides.
acceptance: Startup edits never claim immediate application
Import schema rejects unknown IDs and unsafe values
remaining_obligations: Configuration change, mod removal and conflict capture
Full route omission explanations remain in Inspector; native browser detail shows actual ingredients and effects

requests.title: Useful earlier Bob/Angel productivity research and continuous science demand
requests.proposed_scope: Small early finite tiers and later qualified infinite continuation
requests.rationale: Research should be useful while a factory is growing, not exclusively after the overhaul is finished.
requests.implementation: Derive unlock frontiers and science/lab phases per ecosystem; introduce new finite early tiers without renumbering existing stable IDs; offer an opt-in production load-check view rather than mandatory dummy science sinks.
acceptance: Early/mid/late saves can research intended tiers
No future material in its own prerequisites
Existing progress and queue survive upgrade
Cost and benefit remain meaningful at each tier

requests.title: Pipe, underground-pipe and heat-pipe productivity
requests.proposed_scope: Audit missing family, then admit qualified pipe production
requests.rationale: No named pipe family was found in the inspected modern catalogue; generated omissions and external owners still need checking.
requests.implementation: Audit aliases, settings, ownership and emitted coverage; add a shared pipe family only where absent. Treat 10%/5%/2% as proposed rates, not recovered historical truth. Include casting routes only after process review.
acceptance: Base and overhaul pipe outputs covered
Underground-pipe recipes containing pipes do not create a recovery exploit
remaining_obligations: Deliberate permission policy and weighted recycling economics

requests.title: Longer connected pipeline extent
requests.rationale: MIR already has an extent setting; it must not be sold as new researched range.
requests.implementation: Expose existing control clearly; explain that network extent is constrained by the minimum among connected fluidboxes; audit modded inputs and no-op default.
acceptance: Representative pipe/tank/machine networks agree with UI

requests.title: Longer underground-pipe connection reach
requests.rationale: Underground reach uses a different property and can change connection topology.
requests.implementation: Keep as a separately named optional startup policy or upstream research-hook request; never silently reuse the existing extent multiplier for this.
acceptance: Both endpoints and collision categories tested

requests.title: Weapon firing-speed research
requests.rationale: Native gun-speed exists; MIR already declares rocket, cannon and other speed streams.
requests.implementation: Preserve native owners, check missing ammo categories and saturation, and surface why an existing stream is omitted.
acceptance: Each supported ammo category produces an actual change

requests.title: Handheld weapon range
requests.mechanism: prototype attack range; no direct native equivalent verified
requests.rationale: Artillery range is not a generic handgun/rifle range modifier.
requests.implementation: Request per-force ammo/category range support upstream; avoid swapping guns through hidden per-level prototypes. A startup rebalance is a different optional feature.
acceptance: Preserve weapon item data, ammo, cursor and blueprints if any future adaptation is attempted

requests.title: Cars and tanks use less fuel
requests.rationale: LuaEntity exposes writable consumption_modifier and effectivity_modifier for Car; this supports a promising event-driven implementation without fuel refunds.
requests.implementation: Prototype a measured constant-performance economy mapping, maintain an owned contribution, reconcile on research/build/clone/force/lifecycle changes, and show exact supported entity classes.
acceptance: Acceleration and top speed unchanged within declared tolerance
Multiple forces and other modifier owners handled
remaining_obligations: Multiplayer, clone/quality/surface and save lifecycle qualification
Car probe does not qualify trains, spiders or every modded Car

requests.title: Locomotive and spidertron fuel economy
requests.proposed_scope: Do not infer from Car support
requests.rationale: The verified Car setters do not establish the same facility for rolling stock or spider vehicles.
requests.implementation: Seek exact native/owner adapters. Treat polling remaining fuel or grid-energy refunds as a separate measured experiment, not default implementation.
acceptance: No universal vehicle claim from cars
Multiple fuel transitions and burnt results accounted for before any simulation is admitted

requests.title: Boiler/heating tower and stationary fuel-burning efficiency
requests.rationale: Manufacturing more fuel is not increasing combustion efficiency; generic live effectivity support was not verified.
requests.implementation: Define useful heat/output per fuel separately from power and pollution. Prefer future native modifiers or exact owner integration over tick-based energy refunds.
acceptance: No artificial energy creation labeled native efficiency

requests.title: Faster rocket launch animation
requests.proposed_scope: Investigate native hook; no default 4.2 guarantee
requests.rationale: 2.1 quality can affect animation speed, but that does not itself create a research modifier.
requests.implementation: Separate rocket-part crafting, launch preparation, ascent and cargo delivery; do not fake launches or replace active silos. Optional global startup tuning must be labeled as such.
acceptance: Quality tiers and buffered second rocket

requests.title: Rocket maximum payload
requests.rationale: Rocket payload mass, inventory slots and item stack size are different constraints.
requests.implementation: Use the actual RocketSiloPrototype lift_weight only in a deliberate startup policy; do not change only a display/default constant or item weights and claim researched cargo capacity.
acceptance: Actual mixed cargo fits/exceeds boundary as declared

requests.title: Reduced platform drag
requests.rationale: Writable platform speed is not evidence of a drag modifier.
requests.implementation: Request engine-native drag/thrust-efficiency contribution; keep existing thruster fuel/oxidizer productivity as a separately described benefit.
acceptance: No speed-writing controller represented as aerodynamics

requests.title: Higher quality level-skip probability
requests.proposed_scope: Optional explicit global startup policy only
requests.rationale: The inspected API separates initial improvement from subsequent chain probability; the latter is runtime read-only.
requests.implementation: Keep quality probability model separate from productivity; do not introduce hidden quality levels or rewrite all crafted outputs. Request force-scoped probability hooks.
acceptance: Probability mass and unlocked quality cap tested

requests.title: Higher initial quality probability
requests.rationale: Initial quality success and additional-level skipping are distinct outcomes.
requests.implementation: Assess native force hook on the exact engine; otherwise use existing module mechanics or explicit startup tuning, not broad output interception.
acceptance: No overwrite of another mod result-quality logic
All outputs and productivity cycles consistent

requests.title: Higher uranium-235 probability
requests.proposed_scope: Not equivalent to generic uranium productivity
requests.rationale: Changing U235 probability changes output ratios and enrichment economics.
requests.implementation: Keep as an explicit optional nuclear-process proposal. A researched recipe unlock may be possible but requires new recipe and migration UX; never rewrite all centrifuge output per tick.

requests.title: Larger per-item inventory/chest stacks
requests.rationale: Inventory slots and item stack maximum are different features; the shared item prototype is not force-specific research state.
requests.implementation: Preserve existing inventory-slot research as an explicitly different option. Any startup stack rebalance needs save overflow and compatibility review.

requests.title: Belt stacking research and stacks above four
requests.rationale: A native modifier exists, but configured inserter/loader/belt caps and presentation determine whether extra research has any effect.
requests.implementation: Preserve existing owners, admit only useful finite increments below tested caps. Greater-than-four behavior remains a test-only experiment until visual and transport proof passes.
acceptance: Inserters, loaders, splitters and underground belts
Readability, serialization, throughput and item conservation

requests.title: More wall maximum health
requests.rationale: Current health repair is not an increase in the maximum or survival of a lethal hit.
requests.implementation: Prefer native per-force health/resistance support. Reject damage-event refunds as an undocumented virtual-health system.
acceptance: Future lethal-hit and health-ratio semantics explicit

requests.title: More turret maximum health
requests.rationale: Prototype replacement affects connections, ammo, health and other mods.
requests.implementation: Share the health capability probe; do not generate hidden turret tiers for each research level.
acceptance: No max-health claim based on healing only

requests.title: Faster bot repair, including spidertrons
requests.mechanism: tool speed and prototype repair multiplier
requests.rationale: Tool strength, target repair multiplier, robot travel and robot work are distinct.
requests.implementation: Request target/force robot-repair rate hook; do not remotely add health and claim the bot performed the work. Optional passive repair is a different feature.
acceptance: Repair-pack durability and robot energy conserved

requests.title: Passive repair
requests.rationale: A small scoped service is more credible than simulated max health or instant robot repair.
requests.implementation: Use allowlisted damaged entities, a quiet-time cooldown, capped rate, deterministic round-robin budget and empty-queue unsubscription. Default off; clearly name free regeneration versus resource-consuming repair.
acceptance: Multiple forces/surfaces, deletion and ownership transfer
Other healers compose without exceeding max
remaining_obligations: Multiplayer, clone/quality/surface and save lifecycle qualification
Car probe does not qualify trains, spiders or every modded Car

requests.title: Larger logistic/construction network range
requests.rationale: Network radius can merge separate networks and is not character reach.
requests.implementation: Seek a native scoped contribution with documented network rebuild semantics. Existing robot battery/storage/speed are useful but not this request.

requests.title: Reduced acid slowdown
requests.rationale: Acid damage, movement slowdown and sticker duration must not be conflated.
requests.implementation: Do not delete every sticker or boost global movement. A future allowlisted duration/slowdown adapter must state whether damage duration changes too.

requests.title: Larger handcraft queue
requests.proposed_scope: Do not mistake current count for capacity
requests.rationale: crafting_queue_size is a read-only observed queue size, not a writable maximum.
requests.implementation: Capture the actual UX limit; improve visibility or request native UX support. Existing character crafting speed is a different possible bonus.

requests.title: Artificial tree pollution absorption lifetime
requests.rationale: The pasted request does not identify what owns the artificial tree or its deterioration.
requests.implementation: Separate absorption rate, total capacity and damage/leaf loss; acquire exact owner data and integrate a declared capacity hook. Do not remove arbitrary surface pollution and label it tree capacity.

requests.title: Lower global machine pollution
requests.rationale: Live aggregate machine pollution/effect bonuses are not verified writable per-force controls.
requests.implementation: Request native emission contribution. Do not erase existing pollution chunks or insert hidden beacons as the normal implementation.
acceptance: Pollution per tick and per product distinguished
No ecosystem-wide prototype override disguised as personal research

requests.title: Lower global machine energy use
requests.rationale: The word efficiency is ambiguous; energy use is not identical to direct emissions.
requests.implementation: Name an energy channel separately; prefer native effect modifiers over refunding network electricity.

requests.title: Global machine speed
requests.rationale: Writing progress is not equivalent to engine-native speed across recipes, energy and quality.
requests.implementation: Seek native category/force speed contribution; prohibit invisible module slot consumption, global progress rewriting and hidden per-level machine swaps.

requests.title: Research bonuses with permanent downsides
requests.proposed_scope: Keep permanent research free of compulsory new penalties
requests.rationale: A compulsory irreversible operating penalty can invalidate a functioning factory.
requests.implementation: Research may unlock an optional reversible operating mode later; toggling changes only owned runtime contributions and never unresearches unrelated technologies.

requests.title: Higher-quality beacons consume more energy
requests.rationale: This is a preference about game balance, not missing infinite-research functionality.
requests.implementation: Keep upstream defaults by default. A separate explicit global rebalance can be considered later without making it required for MIR features.
acceptance: Existing saves and power margins reviewed

requests.title: Split MIR into required feature packs
requests.rationale: Internal modularity does not require player-facing dependency fragmentation.
requests.implementation: Bundle official admitted support; default-off optional services must remain dormant. Separate a spin-off only for a genuinely different product, not missing core capability.
acceptance: MIR plus requested overhaul alone works
Disabled services have no recurring work

requests.title: Explain AI/Codex and MD/JSON/YAML guidance
requests.rationale: Explain actual authorship/review and reproducible commands; do not claim all YAML is a required AI standard.
requests.implementation: Document which records are edited versus generated and the standing dev integration workflow. Demonstrate tests and output reproducibility rather than promising infallible agents.
acceptance: New contributor can run ordinary checks
No paid AI service required to reproduce MIR

requests.implementation: Carry phase intent through final science/lab selection; preserve hard-required packs or diagnose conflict. Correct the reversed requested-outcome wording in R1.

requests.title: Exact OmniAB suite-combination intake
requests.rationale: The suite is not one universal dependency graph, and conflict-listed compatibility mods cannot be combined merely to maximize names.
requests.implementation: Acquire, identify and test ordinary installed subsets independently; carry only individually blocked advanced processes beyond 4.2.
acceptance: Each claimed subset has an exact engine, mod, dependency and settings lock
Conflict-listed compatibility mods are never combined into a synthetic universal pack
Claims name the exact qualified subset and actual packaged behavior

requests.title: Canonical OmniAB material and recipe ownership
requests.mechanism: shared material-family admission with one effective owner
requests.proposed_scope: Eligible final OmniAB material routes and aliases
requests.rationale: Bob and Angel material families should be reused against resolved outputs while representation bridges remain distinct from production routes.
requests.implementation: Resolve final outputs and recipes after the suite loads, reuse the generic material family, and preserve native ownership or record a named conflict.
acceptance: Final output identity and every admitted production route are captured
Aliases and representation bridges do not create duplicate bonuses
Every route has one effective owner and an explainable disposition

requests.title: OmniAB rescue-route and progression preservation
requests.rationale: A route intended only to rescue progression must not become the preferred resource shortcut after productivity is applied.
requests.implementation: Classify rescue and ordinary production routes explicitly and exclude or cap rescue paths unless quantitative proof preserves their role.
acceptance: Every admitted route records ordinary, rescue, conversion or representation role
A rescue route cannot dominate intended production under the maximum effective bonus
Early and late progression remain reachable in representative saves

requests.title: OmniAB extraction-tier lifecycle cooperation
requests.proposed_scope: Extraction-tier replacement, retirement and machine contents
requests.rationale: Omnimatter and OmniAB must continue to own tier unlocking, old-tier disabling and machine recipe switching.
requests.implementation: Observe tier transitions and consume their final state without rewriting their lifecycle; validate existing machines and retired recipes through upgrades.
acceptance: Old extraction tiers retire under the suite's own rules
Existing machine contents and recipes survive or migrate under an evidenced policy
MIR never becomes owner of extraction-tier state

requests.title: OmniAB compression and reversible-process restraint
requests.rationale: Representation-only and reversible chains can amplify material when treated as ordinary forward production.
requests.implementation: Preserve them by default and admit only routes with a bounded reviewed process certificate and explicit owner.
acceptance: Compression and reverse routes are identified as one process system
No route is admitted solely because its recipe permission is unset or true
Maximum-bonus loop analysis and recycling behavior are recorded before admission

requests.title: OmniAB planet and alternative-start claim matrix
requests.proposed_scope: Installed planets and alternative starting locations
requests.rationale: Ordinary suite baselines must work before broader starting-location claims are made.
requests.implementation: Qualify named starting locations and installed planet subsets independently after the ordinary OmniAB baseline.
acceptance: Every claim names the starting location and installed planet subset
Science, labs, rescue routes and material progression remain reachable
Unqualified combinations remain explicit rather than inheriting a blanket claim

requests.title: RIC identity and dependency intake
requests.mechanism: exact mod identity and dependency lock
requests.rationale: Graphics dependencies, compatibility layers and gameplay suites must not be conflated.
requests.implementation: Use the internal ID real-industrial-chemistry and acquire each supported mode with its actual dependency closure.
acceptance: The internal mod ID and exact closure are recorded
Graphics-only dependencies are distinguished from gameplay owners
Claims bind an actual containing package and engine

requests.title: RIC mode-aware progression and laboratory proof
requests.proposed_scope: RIC geography, progression and laboratory modes
requests.rationale: Geography and progression settings are independent environment inputs and AAI can change the laboratory frontier.
requests.implementation: Capture the meaningful mode matrix and prove early/late science selection, laboratory handoff and representative save progression.
acceptance: Geography and progression settings are independently identified
Every admitted mode has reachable science and compatible laboratories
AAI laboratory transitions are tested where present

requests.title: RIC manufacturing productivity families
requests.proposed_scope: Eligible RIC metals, alloys, silicon, glass, electronics, polymers and construction outputs
requests.rationale: Actual manufacturing endpoints should reuse proven families instead of accumulating unrelated one-off technology names.
requests.implementation: Resolve final recipes, ownership and progression frontiers and then instantiate only eligible family members.
acceptance: Each family member improves an actual installed manufacturing route
Native owners, alternative routes, returns and effective caps are recorded
Finite and infinite progression produces an effective player benefit

requests.title: RIC closed-loop chemistry and waste handling
requests.proposed_scope: Solvent, catalyst, water recovery and waste routes
requests.rationale: Useful ordinary chemistry and hazardous loops require different admission evidence, while emergency sinks must remain available.
requests.implementation: Admit ordinary forward routes under the normal guard and certificate-gate recovery loops without removing waste or emergency sinks.
acceptance: Closed loops model all inputs, outputs, returns, probabilities and maximum bonuses
Waste and emergency sink behavior is preserved
Blocked individual processes do not prevent qualified ordinary RIC support

requests.title: RIC OpenPit resource and token semantics
requests.proposed_scope: OpenPit deposits, survey samples and state tokens
requests.rationale: Resource prototypes do not by themselves distinguish production mining from survey or deposit-state transitions.
requests.implementation: Identify the owner and lifecycle of every resource or token before applying a mining or manufacturing effect.
acceptance: Production resources are distinguished from survey, sample and state tokens
OpenPit remains owner of deposit state
No bonus duplicates or bypasses a state transition

requests.title: AAI and RIC reconciliation coexistence
requests.proposed_scope: RIC-owned recipes, AAI laboratory handoff and conversion aliases
requests.rationale: Final recipes and laboratories can differ after both suites finish their progression changes.
requests.implementation: Observe the final installed state, preserve RIC and AAI ownership, and bind aliases to one effective MIR family member.
acceptance: RIC-owned final recipes are used instead of stale intermediate identities
Conversion aliases neither duplicate research nor lose the intended endpoint

requests.title: RIC recipe-driven utilities feasibility probe
requests.proposed_scope: Potential boiler, recovery and useful-output processes
requests.rationale: A narrow supported recipe outcome may be feasible, but it is not evidence for universal boiler or heating-tower efficiency.
requests.implementation: Probe actual installed recipe and effect semantics and schedule a later bounded outcome only if the engine exposes a safe owner-compatible mechanism.
acceptance: The exact writable effect and measured useful output are identified
Fuel-use reduction is not inferred from unrelated crafting productivity
An unsupported result is retained as an explicit capability blocker

requests.title: RIC coverage and exclusion explanations
requests.rationale: Players should see coverage decisions inside the same research experience instead of a separate required tool.
requests.implementation: Project route, owner, science, cap and exclusion records through the portable presentation contract.
acceptance: The browser names improved recipes and their effect owner
Science-pack and exclusion reasons are visible in-game
The next level reports whether it can provide an effective benefit

requests.title: Portable in-game research surface
requests.mechanism: host-neutral query core with embedded MIR host and optional companion integration
requests.proposed_scope: Research filtering, sorting, personal hiding, explanations and navigation
requests.rationale: The useful research experience should work inside MIR, be reusable by other mods, and prefer a maintained technology UI extension over a new full tree when the engine cannot extend the vanilla tree directly.
requests.implementation: Refactor a copied-data query and explanation core; keep filters, sorts and personal hidden sets inside the in-game surface; use an OEM-like custom MIR browser and native technology deep links in 4.2; propose or consume a documented upstream extension point for a separately downloadable companion; consider a complete tree and queue replacement in 4.5 only after the integration route is disproved or inadequate.
acceptance: Filter, sort and personal hide controls are available inside the research surface without a mod-settings workflow or external tool
Personal hidden state changes presentation only and never mutates prototype hidden flags, force technology enablement, prerequisites, availability or queue state
Localized technology, material and recipe names are searchable with bounded asynchronous translation work
The selected technology can open in Factorio's native technology GUI on both installed modern engines
The exact API limitation is documented: neither installed modern engine exposes a relative technology-GUI anchor or a supported way to rearrange the vanilla tree
The embedded MIR host and any optional companion share one canonical core and exactly one visible UI host

An existing GUI such as Ultimate Research Queue is extended only through a documented public hook accepted upstream or an equally stable contract; private GUI-tree mutation and source forks are not accepted integration
The companion, if admitted, depends optionally on MIR and its host project; MIR remains self-contained and does not hard-depend on FLib or the companion
Two-player divergent view state, save/reload, removal, configuration change, performance and queue interoperability are qualified
A full OEM+ technology tree and queue overhaul remains an evidence-led 4.5 candidate, not a hidden 4.2 dependency
